Print a Sensitivity Summary

Source: R/smsd_sensitivity.R
smsd_sensitivity_methods.Rd

The *_sensitivity() functions, seq_aipe_smd_sensitivity among them, return a summary that these methods print. The object is a data frame with columns term and value and can be used as one; these methods only change how it is displayed. Each value is formatted on its own, in fixed notation, so that a table mixing a replication count, a coverage proportion, and a mean sample size does not fall into scientific notation as the default data frame print would have it.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'smsd_sensitivity'
format(x, digits = getOption("digits"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'smsd_sensitivity'
print(x, digits = getOption("digits"), ...)

Arguments

x

An object of class "smsd_sensitivity".

digits

Number of significant digits to show. Defaults to getOption("digits"). Stored values are never rounded; this affects display only.

...

Not used.

Value

print() returns its input invisibly. format() returns a character vector, one element per printed line.

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# G is kept small so the example runs quickly; a study to be reported
# deserves G = 10000 or more.
out <- seq_aipe_smd_sensitivity(true_value = 0.5, width = 0.8, G = 20,
                                seed = 113)
out
#> term                   value
#> true_value             0.5
#> target_width           0.8
#> conf_level             0.95
#> replications           20
#> mean_n                 50.6
#> median_n               49.5
#> sd_n                   4.429566
#> mean_width             0.7906421
#> median_width           0.7906787
#> pct_width_within       100
#> coverage               1
#> pct_hit_max_n          0
#> pct_variance_unusable  0
out$value[out$term == "coverage"]
#> [1] 1
